significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(iii) conclusion that the per-sequence “alignment score” quantitatively ranks a sequence’s later trait shift, together with the causal claim that “removing or down-weighting high-alignment sequences suppresses transmission” more efficiently than random or semantic filtering. This would establish both a behavioral phenomenon and a gradient-space mechanism, fixing which examples should carry more influence and which filtering decisions should reduce transmission; that is consequential because Cloud et al., “Subliminal Learning” (2025, arXiv:2507.14805), motivates aggregate gradient movement toward the teacher while reporting failure of semantic filtering. Verified false would distinguishably rule out this local, approximately additive trait-direction account and point toward distributed example interactions or another geometry, although it would not rule out gradient-based mechanisms generally. In the topic-substitution check, subliminal learning alone would not justify this score: the added predictive ordering and targeted causal filtering relation, rather than the topic’s importance, supports an above-median rating.

reach.justification: The named handle is the per-sequence “alignment score,” used as a “gradient-geometry filter” that drops or down-weights examples before student fine-tuning. It is ex ante because it can screen a distillation corpus before transmission occurs, leaving an action window for auditors or practitioners rather than merely explaining an observed failure after the fact. After model-specific re-extraction of the trait direction, the claimed relation still predicts that higher-scoring sequences will induce larger shifts and that removing them will reduce acquisition, so more than a search procedure transfers; however, the conclusion presupposes a known trait direction and does not assert architecture-wide or unknown-trait coverage. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: the topic by itself supplies neither this screening quantity nor a shipping-time filtering decision, while the claim specifically hands those tools to corpus auditors and distillation practitioners.
